# KM-186 — Design parity audit

**Lane:** design · **Complexity:** 2 · **Model:** claude-opus · **Depends on:** KM-180, KM-181, KM-182, KM-183, KM-184, KM-185, KM-187, KM-188 · **Serializes with:** none
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md) · **Design spec:** `docs/design/khala-chat/RECREATION-SPEC.md` §2.1, §21, §22, §25 (the checklist this ticket executes)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** new `apps/web/src/ui/khala/parity.browser.spec.ts`, new `apps/web/src/ui/khala/parity-masks.ts`, new `docs/design/khala-chat/PARITY-REPORT.md`, `docs/design/khala-chat/reference/screens/**` (regenerated only by `capture.mjs`). Small drift fixes are allowed **only** in the CSS files owned by KM-180..185/187 (`apps/web/src/ui/khala/*.css`, `features/agent-confirm/agent-confirm.css`, `landing/landing.css` `.signin`). Each fix is listed in the report with its ticket of origin.

## Outcome

- An automated, repeatable parity check proves the Khala app matches the imported Claude Design. It compares the KM-188 fixture against the design references at **1440, 1100, 900, 760 and 390 px**, in **dark and light**, and in the key states.
- It also checks computed styles, the **operator font directive**, the D1–D5 fixes, the M1 matrix (§22) and the Sign In change (§19).
- Its output is `docs/design/khala-chat/PARITY-REPORT.md`: a table per check with pass/fail, diff ratio and screenshot paths, the fixes applied, and any remaining operator decisions.

## Context and evidence

- Spec §25 is the checklist. The references are `docs/design/khala-chat/reference/screens/fullbleed-*.png` and `reference/computed-styles.json`, regenerated from the real design with `docs/design/khala-chat/reference/capture.mjs`.
- **Operator directive:** UI text uses the Claude Design font stacks exactly; Bungee appears only on the logo wordmark (spec §2.1).
- The fixture: `apps/web/conversation-fixture.html` (KM-188), with query parameters `theme`, `view`, `roster`, `chips`, `detail`, `pop`, `failed`, `empty` and `draft`.
- Browser specs build with Vite and drive Chromium through `@playwright/test`, following the pattern in `apps/web/src/ui/conversation/detail.browser.spec.ts:8-30`. Run them with `pnpm --filter @khala/web test:browser`.

## Scope

1. **Re-capture the references on the same machine as the comparison, so the rasterizer matches:**
   `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE_PKG=$(node -p "require.resolve('playwright-core/package.json',{paths:[require.resolve('@playwright/test',{paths:['apps/web']})]})") node docs/design/khala-chat/reference/capture.mjs`
2. **`parity.browser.spec.ts`:** build the fixture (the detail-spec pattern) and, for each width × theme × state, screenshot the fixture and compare it to `reference/screens/fullbleed-<w>-<theme>-<state>.png`. Compare with a small inline pixel diff: load both PNGs into a page `<canvas>` with `page.evaluate`, then count pixels whose per-channel delta is greater than 16. Add no new dependency. The threshold is `diffPixels / totalPixels ≤ 0.02`, after applying masks.

   | Width | States |
   |---|---|
   | 1440 | thread, roster, chips, detail-agent, detail-human, pop-new, pop-invite, pop-add-agent, empty-channel, failed-send, draft |
   | 1100, 900, 760 | thread (plus list at ≤900) |
   | 390 | thread, list, roster, chips, detail-agent, pop-invite |

3. **Masks** (`parity-masks.ts`): one exported entry per §22 "Omit" item visible in the design reference. Each entry has a selector or box, a reason, and the §22 row. They cover:
   - `.kh-ask` (the "Your agent?" chip)
   - the header `.kh-badge`
   - the roster Requests group and `.kh-crw` crowns
   - `.kh-rai-p` progress
   - `.kh-st` dots
   - kebabs
   - the `.kh-hacts` gear
   - the state-channel rows in the list (`Infra on-call`, `0.8 launch room`, `Design crit`)
   - `.kh-react`
   - detail Working-on/kv/Open-ticket regions
   - the `.kh-d-agent > i` percentages

   Masks are boxes painted on **both** images before diffing. Never mask a region that M1 renders.
4. **Computed-style assertions** at 1440-dark, 1440-light and 390-dark: for every selector in `reference/computed-styles.json`, compare `color`, `background-color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-family`, `padding`, `border-radius`, `border`, `line-height` and `letter-spacing` **exactly**, and the box within ±2px. Skip selectors that are §22-omitted, and skip boxes that depend on dataset text length (documented in the report).
5. **Font directive check** (§25.1): on every fixture state, the app's `/conversations` and `/channels/…` pages (mocked ports, as in `features/timeline/timeline.browser.spec.ts`), the sign-in redirect card and the confirm page (KM-185):
   - Walk all elements under `.khala-app`.
   - Assert `getComputedStyle(el).fontFamily` starts with `"Space Grotesk"` or `"JetBrains Mono"`, **except** `.kh-brand .wm`, which must start with `Bungee`.
   - Assert no other element computes to Bungee.
   - Assert `document.querySelector('link[href^="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bungee&family=Space+Grotesk:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"]')` exists.
6. **Behaviour and structure assertions:** spec §25 items 5–11. These cover run classes; `.me`/agent ownership; the single receipt and never "Read"; chip order, toggle threshold and grid; D1 colours (dark human chip `hsl(oh 70% 72%)`); D2 (no strip at 390); D3 (.78rem); D5 (32×32); the M1 matrix (Omit absent, Disabled carrying `disabled` and `title="Coming soon"`); and Sign In (landing link `href`, `.tool-btn` metrics, no "Open Khala app", a signed-out `/conversations` navigating to the login URL without a sign-in page).
7. **Accessibility:** inject axe-core from the existing devDependencies if present. If it is not installed, record "not run" in the report. Do **not** add dependencies without asking.
8. **Drift fixes:** when a check fails because of CSS drift in a design-lane CSS file, fix it in place and record the line and ticket. Behaviour or DOM failures are **not** fixed here: file them in the report as blocking, with the owning ticket.
9. **Report:** write `docs/design/khala-chat/PARITY-REPORT.md` with: date, commit, environment, each check's result, diff ratios per screenshot, masks used, fixes applied and open items. The report must restate the D1 decision (§21) and the operator's sign-off status.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning anything, and changing any component's DOM or behaviour (owned by KM-180..188).
- Updating `@aiur/components`.
- CI wiring of this spec. It runs under `test:browser` locally; a CI gate is a follow-up for the Executor.

## Contract and invariants

- References are regenerated, never hand-edited.
- Masks always state their §22 row.
- The threshold is 0.02. Raising it requires an Executor decision, recorded in the report.

## Implementation pointers

**Create:** `apps/web/src/ui/khala/parity.browser.spec.ts`, `apps/web/src/ui/khala/parity-masks.ts`, `docs/design/khala-chat/PARITY-REPORT.md`

**Modify (drift fixes only):** the design-lane CSS files named in **Exclusive write surfaces**

### Steps

1. Run the capture (step 1 of **Scope**).
2. Write the masks, then the spec.
3. Run, fix drift, and repeat until everything is green or blocked.
4. Write the report.

## Test scenarios

`apps/web/src/ui/khala/parity.browser.spec.ts`. Each item is an enumerated test:
- `screens: <w>-<theme>-<state>` for every combination in step 2 of **Scope** (about 40 tests).
- `computed: <viewport-theme>: <selector>` for every non-omitted selector.
- `fonts: <page>` for the fixture states, the app routes, the sign-in redirect and the confirm page.
- `runs`, `ownership`, `receipt`, `chips`, `D1`, `D2`, `D3`, `D5`, `m1-matrix`, `sign-in`.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @khala/web test:browser` (the parity spec included)
- `pnpm typecheck`

**Done when:**
- Every check passes or is listed as a blocking item with its owning ticket.
- `PARITY-REPORT.md` is committed in the ticket's PR.

## Risks and stop conditions

- If more than 10% of screen comparisons exceed 0.02 because of font rasterization differences, not real drift (for example a uniform sub-pixel offset), stop and ask the Executor whether to compare inside the pinned `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble` image instead.
- If a §22 omission leaves an obvious layout hole versus the design (for example the empty `.kh-hacts` gear slot), report it for an operator decision. Do not invent UI.

## Complexity rationale

2: a test harness and a report, with no product behaviour.
